title: Canonical coordinate-tower normalization data
statement: Fix a finite coefficient datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], a level $n\geq0$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B$. Put $X_r=\mathbf A^r_B$, with ordered projection $p_r$, zero vector $z_r$, last-coordinate projection $q_r$ and section $s_r$ [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. Write $W_r=A_{X_r}(r)[2r]$ for the ordered Tate power. Its canonical ordinary antecedent is $R\nu_*W_r$, and its comparison is the comparison counit. Let $v_r:W_{r+1}\to Rq_r^!W_r$ be the actual affine-line comparison after the ordered source identification. Define LineLaw(c) to assert invertibility and naturality of those comparisons on finite-Tor etale-origin inputs for $r<c$. Define $e_{q_r}:Rs_r^!Rq_r^!W_r\to W_r$ from the inverse mate of the fixed compact-support compositor, equality $q_rs_r=1$, and inverse identity unit. Define $d_r^{-1}:Rz_r^!Rs_r^!W_{r+1}\to Rz_{r+1}^!W_{r+1}$ by the same inverse mate and $z_{r+1}=s_rz_r$. For any family $u_r:W_r\to Rs_r^!W_{r+1}$ define $\theta_0$ by the canonical identity unit and $\theta_{r+1}=d_r^{-1}Rz_r^!(u_r)\theta_r$. Define the actual projection comparison at $W_r$, its adjunct augmentation, the closed adjunct of $\theta_r$ using proper direct image, and the compact source identification $Rp_{r!}z_{r*}A_B\simeq A_B$ from the fixed composition, equality, and identity isomorphisms. These are the existing constructions, relocated verbatim, including their proved finite-Tor origin properties. No normalization conclusion is part of the definitions.

proof.text: The constructions are the previously recorded canonical maps. For the preserved target_properties theorem, the finite Tate line is etale locally free and flat by the finite-etale twist-line result. Its shifted degree-zero complex is constructible with finite Tor amplitude. Induct on tensor powers using tensor stability and the canonical monoidal comparison; the zero case is the coefficient unit. Comparison detects the Tor interval, and its adjunction identifies the canonical Rnu_* antecedent and counit. The remaining endpoint equalities and recurrences are the literal constructors specified above.
